newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-YORKSHIRE ANNOUNCE SURPRISE MOVE TO QUIT HEADINGLEY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-YORKSHIRE ANNOUNCE SURPRISE MOVE TO QUIT HEADINGLEY.

text.p: Headingley, one of England's best known cricket grounds, looked certain to disappear from the test circuit after Yorkshire announced plans on Monday to move to a new 50 million pounds ($78 million) stadium near Wakefield.
The surprise announcement signalled the end of more than 100 years' association between the county club and the Leeds ground.
Yorkshire are only tenants at Headingley and they have become increasingly frustrated over their inability to capitalise fully on test match proceeds or to expand the limited facilities.

Yorkshire president Sir Lawrence Byford said: "At long last, our distinguished club with its outstanding cricketing heritage is on the threshold of owning its own cricket stadium together with the community facilities that will enable it to progress cricket even further throughout Yorkshire."
The new 25,000-capacity all-seater stadium is to be built on a site near Wakefield in the south of the county and Yorkshire hope to start playing there in four years.
"I will really regret leaving Headingley, but with the best will in the world, the ground is becoming tired," Byford said.

"It would need a vast amount of investment to retain test match status, and I believe the money needed to buy the ground and then enhance it to the necessary degree would be almost impossible to raise.

"Of course, there are no guarantees in this world, but our plans have the full support of the Test and County Cricket Board, who told me in a recent letter: `It is unthinkable that Yorkshire should not be able to stage test cricket'."
